verses.zh: 成群的民（原文是女子）哪，现在你要聚集成队；因为仇敌围攻我们，要用杖击打以色列审判者的脸。
verses.en: (4:14)[NOTE:1] But now slash yourself,[NOTE:2] daughter surrounded by soldiers![NOTE:3] We are besieged!With a scepter[NOTE:4] they strike Israel’s ruler[NOTE:5] on the side of his face.
notes: Beginning with 5:1, the verse numbers through 5:15 in the English Bible differ by one from the verse numbers in the Hebrew text (BHS), with 5:1 ET = 4:14 HT, 5:2 ET = 5:1 HT, 5:3 ET = 5:2 HT, etc., through 5:15 ET = 5:14 HT. From 6:1 the verse numbers in the English Bible and the Hebrew Bible are again the same.

The Hebrew verb גָדַד (gadad) can be translated “slash yourself” or “gather in troops.” A number of English translations are based on the latter meaning (e.g., NASB, NIV, NLT).sn Slash yourself. Slashing one’s body was a form of mourning. See Deut 14:1; 1 Kgs 18:28; Jer 16:6; 41:5; 47:5.
Heb “daughter of a troop of warriors.”sn The daughter surrounded by soldiers is an image of the city of Jerusalem under siege (note the address “Daughter Jerusalem” in 4:8).
Striking a king with a scepter, a symbol of rulership, would be especially ironic and humiliating. tn Or “staff”; KJV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT “rod”; CEV “stick”; NCV “club.”
Traditionally, “the judge of Israel” (so KJV, NASB).

verses.zh: 伯利恒的以法他啊，你在犹大诸城中为小，将来必有一位从你那里出来，在以色列中为我作掌权的；他的根源从亘古，从太初就有。
verses.en: (5:1) As for you, Bethlehem Ephrathah,[NOTE:1] seemingly insignificant[NOTE:2] among the clans of Judah—from you a king will emerge who will rule over Israel on my behalf,[NOTE:3] one whose origins[NOTE:4] are in the distant past.[NOTE:5]
notes: Ephrathah is either an alternate name for Bethlehem or the name of the district in which Bethlehem was located. See Ruth 4:11.map For location of Bethlehem see Map5-B1; Map7-E2; Map8-E2; Map10-B4.
Heb “being small.” Some omit לִהְיוֹת (liheyot, “being”) because it fits awkwardly and appears again in the next line.
Heb “from you for me one will go out to be a ruler over Israel.”
Heb “his goings out.” The term may refer to the ruler’s origins (cf. NAB, NIV, NRSV, NLT) or to his activities.

In riddle-like fashion this verse alludes to David, as the references to Bethlehem and to his ancient origins/activities indicate. The passage anticipates the second coming of the great king to usher in a new era of national glory for Israel. Other prophets are more direct and name this coming ideal ruler “David” (Jer 30:9; Ezek 34:23-24; 37:24-25; Hos 3:5). Of course, this prophecy of “David’s” second coming is actually fulfilled through his descendant, the Messiah, who will rule in the spirit and power of his famous ancestor and bring to realization the Davidic royal ideal in an even greater way than the historical David (see Isa 11:1, 10; Jer 33:15).tn Heb “from the past, from the days of antiquity.” Elsewhere both phrases refer to the early periods in the history of the world or of the nation of Israel. For מִקֶּדֶם (miqqedem, “from the past”) see Neh 12:46; Pss 74:12; 77:11; Isa 45:21; 46:10. For מִימֵי עוֹלָם (mime ʿolam, “from the days of antiquity”) see Isa 63:9, 11; Amos 9:11; Mic 7:14; Mal 3:4. In Neh 12:46 and Amos 9:11 the Davidic era is in view.

verses.zh: 耶和华必将以色列人交付敌人，直等那生产的妇人生下子来。那时掌权者（原文是他）其余的弟兄必归到以色列人那里。
verses.en: So the Lord[NOTE:1] will hand the people of Israel[NOTE:2] over to their enemies[NOTE:3] until the time when the woman in labor[NOTE:4] gives birth.[NOTE:5] Then the rest of the king’s[NOTE:6] countrymen will returnto be reunited with the people of Israel.[NOTE:7]
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (the Lord) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “them”; the referent (the people of Israel) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
The words “to their enemies” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
The woman in labor. Personified, suffering Jerusalem is the referent. See 4:9-10.
Gives birth. The point of the figurative language is that Jerusalem finally finds relief from her suffering. See 4:10.
Heb “his”; the referent (the king) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

Heb “to the sons of Israel.” The words “be reunited with” are supplied in the translation for clarity.sn The rest of the king’s countrymen are the coming king’s fellow Judahites, while the people of Israel are the northern tribes. The verse pictures the reunification of the nation under the Davidic king. See Isa 11:12-13; Jer 31:2-6, 15-20; Ezek 37; Hos 1:11; 3:5.

verses.zh: 他必起来，倚靠耶和华的大能，并耶和华―他　神之名的威严，牧养他的羊群。他们要安然居住；因为他必日见尊大，直到地极。
verses.en: He will assume his post[NOTE:1] and shepherd the people[NOTE:2] by the Lord’s strength,by the sovereign authority of the Lord his God.[NOTE:3] They will live securely,[NOTE:4] for at that time he will be honored[NOTE:5] even in the distant regions of[NOTE:6] the earth.
notes: Heb “stand up”; NAB “stand firm”; NASB “will arise.”
The words “the people” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
Heb “by the majesty of the name of the Lord his God.”
The words “in peace” are supplied in the translation for clarification. Perhaps וְיָשָׁבוּ (veyashavu, “and they will live”) should be emended to וְשָׁבוּ (veshavu, “and they will return”).
Heb “be great.”
Or “to the ends of.”

verses.zh: 这位必作我们的平安。当亚述人进入我们的地境，践踏宫殿的时候，我们就立起七个牧者，八个首领攻击他。
verses.en: He will give us peace.[NOTE:1] Should the Assyrians try to invade our landand attempt to set foot in our fortresses,[NOTE:2] we will send[NOTE:3] against them seven[NOTE:4] shepherd-rulers,[NOTE:5] make that eight commanders.[NOTE:6]
notes: Heb “and this one will be peace”; ASV “and this man shall be our peace” (cf. Eph 2:14).
Some prefer to read “in our land,” emending the text to בְּאַדְמָתֵנוּ (beʾadmatenu).
Heb “raise up.”
The numbers seven and eight here symbolize completeness and emphasize that Israel will have more than enough military leadership and strength to withstand the Assyrian advance.
Heb “shepherds.”
Heb “and eight leaders of men.”

verses.zh: 他们必用刀剑毁坏亚述地和宁录地的关口。亚述人进入我们的地境践踏的时候，他必拯救我们。
verses.en: They will rule[NOTE:1] the land of Assyria with the sword,the land of Nimrod[NOTE:2] with a drawn sword.[NOTE:3] Our king[NOTE:4] will rescue us from the Assyriansshould they attempt to invade our landand try to set foot in our territory.
notes: Or perhaps “break”; or “defeat.”
According to Gen 10:8-12, Nimrod, who was famous as a warrior and hunter, founded Assyria.
The MT reads בִּפְתָחֶיהָ (biftakheha) “in her gates,” but the text should be emended to בַּפְּתִיחָה (bappetikhah) “with a drawn sword.”
Heb “he”; the referent (the coming king) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 雅各余剩的人必在多国的民中，如从耶和华那里降下的露水，又如甘霖降在草上；不仗赖人力，也不等候世人之功。
verses.en: Those survivors from[NOTE:1] Jacob will live[NOTE:2] in the midst of many nations.[NOTE:3] They will be like the dew the Lord sends,like the rain on the grass,that does not hope for men to comeor wait around for humans to arrive.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “the remnant of” (also in v. 8).
Heb “will be.”
This could mean “(scattered) among the nations” (cf. CEV, NLT) or “surrounded by many nations” (cf. NRSV).

Heb “that does not hope for man, and does not wait for the sons of men.”sn Men wait eagerly for the dew and the rain, not vice versa. Just as the dew and rain are subject to the Lord, not men, so the remnant of Israel will succeed by the supernatural power of God and not need the support of other nations. There may even be a military metaphor here. Israel will overwhelm their enemies, just as the dew completely covers the grass (see 2 Sam 17:12). This interpretation would be consistent with the image of v. 7.

verses.zh: 雅各余剩的人必在多国多民中，如林间百兽中的狮子，又如少壮狮子在羊群中。他若经过就必践踏撕裂，无人搭救。
verses.en: Those survivors from Jacob will live among the nations,in the midst of many peoples.They will be like a lion among the animals of the forest,like a young lion among the flocks of sheep,which attacks when it passes through.It rips its prey[NOTE:1] and there is no one to stop it.[NOTE:2]
notes: The words “its prey” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
Heb “and there is no deliverer.”

verses.zh: 愿你的手举起，高过敌人！愿你的仇敌都被剪除！
verses.en: Lift your hand triumphantly against your adversaries;[NOTE:1] may all your enemies be destroyed![NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “let your hand be lifted against your adversaries.”
Heb “be cut off.”

verses.zh: 耶和华说：到那日，我必从你中间剪除马匹，毁坏车辆，
verses.en: “In that day,” says the Lord, “I will destroy[NOTE:1] your horses from your midstand smash your chariots.
notes: Heb “cut off” (also in the following verse).

verses.zh: 也必从你国中除灭城邑，拆毁一切的保障，
verses.en: I will destroy the cities of your landand tear down all your fortresses.

verses.zh: 又必除掉你手中的邪术；你那里也不再有占卜的。
verses.en: I will remove the sorcery[NOTE:1] that you practice,[NOTE:2] and you will no longer have omen readers living among you.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “magic charms” (so NCV, TEV); NIV, NLT “witchcraft”; NAB “the means of divination.” The precise meaning of this Hebrew word is uncertain, but note its use in Isa 47:9, 12.
Heb “from your hands.”
Heb “and you will not have omen-readers.”

verses.zh: 我必从你中间除灭雕刻的偶像和柱像，你就不再跪拜自己手所造的。
verses.en: I will remove your idols and sacred pillars from your midst;you will no longer worship what your own hands made.

verses.zh: 我必从你中间拔出木偶，又毁灭你的城邑。
verses.en: I will uproot your images of Asherah[NOTE:1] from your midstand destroy your idols.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “Asherah poles.”sn Asherah was a leading deity of the Canaanite pantheon, wife/sister of El and goddess of fertility. She was commonly worshiped at shrines in or near groves of evergreen trees, or, failing that, at places marked by wooden poles. These were to be burned or cut down (Deut 12:3; 16:21; Judg 6:25, 28, 30; 2 Kgs 18:4). The Lord states that he will destroy these images, something the Israelites themselves should have done but failed to do.
The MT reads “your cities,” but many emend the text to צִרֶיךָ (tsirekha, “your images”) or עֲצַבֶּיךָ (ʿatsbbekha, “your idols”).

verses.zh: 我也必在怒气和忿怒中向那不听从的列国施报。
verses.en: With furious anger I will carry out vengeanceon the nations that do not obey me.”
